players.name: António João Pereira de Albuquerque Tavares da Silva

1.headline: Haaland was everyone's captain and still managed to disappoint almost everyone
1.introduction: Gameweek 1 served up exactly what we wanted: a ridiculous 72-71 thriller, one manager accidentally winning by pretending his team was deliberate, and enough identical captain choices to suggest half of you read the same five-minute Twitter thread. Notes: Patrick tops the table with 76, Tom enjoys being bottom with 47, and Woolly has already reminded us money can buy a decent score (and a huge margin).

matches.title: Richard 56 v Prince Majid Rd FC 57
matches.text: Rich vs Rami was a one-point disagreement that probably started over who gets the loo first. Both managers put Bruno on captain duty and both got a grand total of four from it — perfectly reasonable behaviour if your ambition is to be boringly consistent. Rich's João Pedro (11) did some heavy lifting but it wasn't enough. Rami sneaks it 57-56 and gets to claim a moral victory about spreadsheet strategy while the rest of us glare at two identical captaincies.

matches.title: Humorous Name United 72 v Roped in again 71
matches.text: The highest-scoring match of the week and absolute chaos. Rob edged Paul by a point in a 143-point shootout — brilliant, exhausting, and completely unnecessary. Paul’s Haaland armband (double) produced four effective points; Rob’s Bruno captain managed the same. You couldn’t write it: both managers lean on the obvious picks and it still comes down to coin-flips and bench order. Rob wins, Paul loses by one and will now spend the week explaining how his transfers were 'on brand'.

matches.title: Change Name FC 67 v Bielsa's Babes 76
matches.text: Patrick decided to open the season by taking the biscuit — 76 and top of the pile. David had a respectable 67 but that wasn’t enough; Patrick’s João Pedro (11) and the usual suspects delivered. Both managers were among those who trusted Haaland with the captaincy and thus celebrated a rather modest return. Patrick can now enjoy being a Leeds fan with a points cushion; the rest of you can either be jealous or suspicious of his off-season.

matches.title: el Guapo 47 v BeLucky Again 51
matches.text: Tom somehow scored the lowest total of the week (47) despite having Granit Xhaka sitting on the bench with nine points — a decision that will be analysed and mocked in equal measure. Kev turned up from his golf round with 51 and a narrow win; fair play, that’s the kind of efficient, slightly smug start Kevin likes. Tom, meanwhile, will be reassured only by the fact no-one else had a catastrophe big enough to make this week look worse than it already is.

matches.title: FC Dangerous 50 v Seattle Scorchers 50
matches.text: A draw. Fifty each. Rob and Andrew both end the week perfectly average and perfectly aligned. Both captained Haaland for double points and received the same tiny consolation return, which is the kind of symmetry that feels unfairly poetic. This match was the narrowest margin possible — nothing to split them; both get a point and both go home to practice slightly different hand-wringing routines.

matches.title: ChampagneSuperRovers 55 v Atletico Waspo 59
matches.text: Foz’s 59 nudged James off the mark. Another manager who trusted the usual suspects and came away with a tidy not-quite-great score. James will rue Haaland’s meagre double return like half the league; Ben quietly collects three points and moves on with his week. No drama, no big brain moves, just a clean little win.

matches.title: Woolbrohampton 71 v Turf Less 50
matches.text: Biggest winning margin of the week and the result everyone expected someone with money would achieve: Woolly put together 71 and beat Martyn by 21. Martyn’s Cole Palmer actually scored 13 but that couldn’t stop the rout; Woolbrohampton’s João Pedro again chipped in with double figures. Martyn’s Burnleyness remains intact but this scoreline is a reminder that being a fan of a rubbish club does not exempt you from getting mugged off in FPL.

awards.award: The Highest Scoring Weekend (Stop Showing Off) Award
awards.text: 76 points and top of the official table — Patrick strolls in at the weekend like he’s buying rounds for everyone. Fair play, he made the most of the predictable picks and tucked the points away.
72-71. The highest-scoring match of GW1 and a one-point victory. Rob wins the sort of match that leaves Paul reassessing life choices and the rest of us soggy from the sweat of it.

awards.award: The Biggest Margin (Smash and Grab) Award
awards.text: A 21-point win is the GW1 statement no-one asked for. Woolly flexes a big margin and we are all reminded that money and taste can coexist in one team sheet.

Tom scored the week’s lowest total (47) while Granit Xhaka sat on the bench with nine points. That bench decision will be replayed in group chat for at least three days. Painful, but entertaining for the rest of us.

1.table_commentary: The official Super 8s table is already telling a story: Patrick (Bielsa's Babes) leads with 76, followed by Rob's Humorous Name United (72) and Woolbrohampton (71). All three have three league points — the placings are decided by total FPL points scored, which is why Patrick gets the bragging rights. Mid-table is a scramble of one-match wonders and a couple of 50-point draws (Watson and Crystal) who’ve earned a solitary point each. Down at the sharp end, Tom (el Guapo) sits on 47 and will be getting a stream of unsolicited transfer advice by Tuesday.

preview.fixture: Prince Majid Rd FC (Rami) v Woolbrohampton (Woolly)
preview.text: Rami hosts Woolly next — a tasty little clash. Ben arrives in form and high on confidence after a 21-point win; Rami will need to be at his spreadsheety best to stop Woolly building momentum. If Rami wants to upset the applecart he'll have to do it without any signs of sports-washing — this one looks like a challenge for manager nous over bank balance.

Two managers looking for a response. Martyn was on the wrong end of a 21-point defeat and James lost by four — both will fancy a bounce-back. Martyn's Cole Palmer showed up with 13 already; if he repeats that it might be curtains for James unless James can stop benching points or find a surprise captain that isn’t the rest of the league’s default.

preview.fixture: Bielsa's Babes (Paddy) v Humorous Name United (Rob)
preview.text: Patrick vs Rob is GW2’s early headline: 76 vs 72 from GW1. Both managers showed they know how to rack up points and neither is shy about the predictable picks. Expect another high-scoring affair — or at least a tense one. This one could decide who has the psychological edge going into September.

1.closing: That’s GW1 done. Plenty to argue about, a clutch of identical captain decisions to mock, and a table that already gives people reasons to be smug or sulky. Get your transfers in, stop copying the bloke with the most followers, and prepare for more of this nonsense next week.
